purpose: Estimate whether LLM or hybrid LLM multi-agent simulation is economically feasible compared with the existing rule-based ABM baseline.

pricing_source.note: Prices are assumptions for feasibility estimation and should be rechecked before final thesis experiments.

experiment_design.note: calls = scenarios * rounds_per_scenario * replications * llm_agents * calls_per_agent_round

architectures.name: rule_based_abm
architectures.description: Current thesis baseline. Agents follow rules/probabilistic behavior. No LLM call.

architectures.name: hybrid_llm_abm
architectures.description: Rule-based customer/fraud/system agents; LLM only for analyst and policy-maker interpretation/decision support.

architectures.name: full_llm_abm
architectures.description: Several agents use LLM reasoning, including customer/fraud/analyst/policy-maker/system narrative agents.

interpretation.technical_feasible_if: Cost per scenario and latency remain small enough to run repeated scenario tests.
interpretation.economic_feasible_if: Expected improvement in policy net benefit is greater than token cost.
interpretation.recommended_next_step: Run a small empirical pilot with API usage logs or LangSmith to replace token assumptions with measured values.
